subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — follow-up & GPU/throughput clarification
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@nimbus-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — follow-up & GPU/throughput clarification

Hi Sara — great to meet today, thanks for walking us through Nimbus's fraud-prevention and payments flows. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can size Dedicated correctly.

Recap (from our call)
- Primary deployment preference: Dedicated capacity (data residency + predictable throughput)
- Primary workload: realtime authorization and risk scoring via a generation model + some embedding-based retrieval for historical context
- Peak window: US business hours, sustained traffic for ~10h/day with spikes during payroll cycles

Questions we need answers to before we finalize a capacity proposal:
1) Target traffic: can you confirm expected peak requests-per-second (RPS)? In the call you mentioned ~100–150 RPS; is 120 RPS a reasonable peak number?
2) Token mix: what is the average input (prompt) and output (response) token length? Example: 300 tokens in + 500 tokens out = 800 tokens total.
3) Concurrency: how many concurrent active sessions do you expect during peak? (sessions that hold KV cache)
4) Model & latency SLO: are you planning to use an open generative model (e.g., LlamaX-13B) or a larger family? Target 95th percentile latency target for full responses?
5) GPU preference: any restrictions — do you require H100-class hardware, or is A100 acceptable if it reduces cost?
6) Private network: if we size for Private/VPC later, do you have bandwidth/egress constraints we should account for?

Attachments: I’m attaching a short dedicated sizing template (redwood_dedicated_sizing_template.xlsx) to populate the numbers above — if you can fill and send back we’ll convert to a capacity proposal. Also attaching our standard timing/pricing stub for context.

Proposed next steps:
- Sara: confirm the six items above + attach a short traffic sample if available
- Ben/Marissa: produce initial capacity proposal once we have numbers (aiming 48h turnaround)
- Follow-up call: schedule a 30-min session next week to review the proposal and PoC scope

Thanks — I’ll hold on final sizing until I get the numbers.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_sizing_template.xlsx, example_sla.pdf
From: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@nimbus-payments.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: DevOps Team <infra@nimbus-payments.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 11:18:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — follow-up & GPU/throughput clarification

Ben — thanks for the recap and the template. Answers below (and I attached a small CSV with observed traffic slices: infra_profile.csv).

1) Peak RPS: 120 RPS sustained for ~20 minute bursts, baseline 40–60 RPS outside bursts.
2) Token mix (average): prompt 350 tokens, response 450 tokens -> ~800 tokens/request. During higher-granularity fraud checks some requests go to ~1,200 tokens.
3) Concurrency: roughly 60 concurrent sessions that keep context KV cache warm; ephemeral sessions spike to ~150 during bursts.
4) Model & latency SLO: prefer a performant open model in the 13B–70B family (we're evaluating LlamaX-13B and Mistral-70B). 95p latency target: <=450ms for responses up to 500 tokens; we can accept occasional deviations for longer responses.
5) GPU: H100 preferred if available (we prioritize latency), but we are open to A100 if you can demonstrate it meets the SLO for our token profile.
6) Network: for Private/VPC option — we have a 10 Gbps dedicated link available and strict egress reporting requirements.

Timeline: we want a PoC in the next 4 weeks; would need a ballpark committed quote for capacity to pull internal approvals.

Thanks — cc'ing our infra lead for bandwidth details.

Cheers,
Sara Jensen
Head of AI, Nimbus Payments
sara.jensen@nimbus-payments.com | +1 (646) 555-0198

Attachment: infra_profile.csv

Subject: Nimbus follow-up: preliminary Dedicated capacity proposal (internal)

Team — quick internal note after Sara's reply (see infra_profile.csv). High-level ask: produce a preliminary capacity and cost estimate we can send as a committed ballpark for their internal approvals and to scope a 4-week PoC.

Key numbers from Nimbus:
- Peak: 120 RPS bursts; baseline 40–60 RPS
- Token mix average: ~800 tokens/request; some up to 1,200 tokens
- Concurrency: 60 warm sessions, spikes to 150 ephemeral
- Model family: 13B–70B (LlamaX-13B and Mistral-70B under consideration)
- 95p latency target: <=450ms for responses up to 500 tokens
- Preferred HW: H100 preferred, A100 acceptable if meets SLO
- Private/VPC: 10 Gbps link and egress reporting needed

Initial sizing hypothesis (ballpark) — Marissa/Vivek, please validate:
- Option A (performance): 8 x H100 full nodes with Redwood runtime optimizations, autoscale headroom for bursts (predictive scaling + burst buffer). Expected sustained token throughput ~75k tokens/s across the pool with batching, should cover 120 RPS at ~800 tokens/request with headroom.
- Option B (cost-optimized): 12 x A100-80GB nodes + heavier batching + quantization profile for LlamaX-13B. Expected sustained token throughput ~60k tokens/s; may hit SLO for 95p at 500 tokens but requires careful batching config and low queueing.

Next actions:
- Marissa: confirm throughput estimates per GPU class for the two model families (LlamaX-13B, Mistral-70B) using our profiling knobs (quant / kernel choices). Slide me numbers for both Option A and B by EOD Mon (Mar 16).
- Vivek: draft a short customer-facing one-pager comparing the two options (performance vs cost) + preliminary PoC runbook (include monitoring hooks: token-level cost, 95p latency, KV cache hit rate).
- Rishi: start a HubSpot deal update (NIM-2026-003) with these numbers and capture approval gate for committed quote.

I’ll pull together a short PDF (initial_capacity_proposal.pdf) to send Nimbus once we validate the numbers. Aim to have a customer call next Wed to present.

Thanks — Ben
